title: Statistical Learning Theory
conclusions: Foundational textbook establishing VC theory and structural risk minimization as the basis of statistical learning theory.

Introduces/popularizes the transductive inference setting: given labeled training data plus a specific unlabeled (test) set, the goal is to label that fixed set directly rather than to infer a general rule (induction).
Develops generalization bounds and principles (VC dimension, capacity control) that motivate both the inductive and transductive learning paradigms.

Widely cited as the canonical origin of the transduction concept in the ML literature, alongside later refinements by Vapnik, Gammerman and Vovk (1998, UAI, 'Learning by Transduction') and Joachims (1999) for transductive SVMs.
our_use: main.tex ~line 217-218, paragraph 'Transductive and set-level constraints': 'Transductive inference reasons about a fixed unlabeled test set \citep{vapnik1998statistical,joachims1999transductive}, and soft set-level targets have long existed there...'. The citation supports the general claim that transductive inference (reasoning about a fixed unlabeled test set, as opposed to inductive generalization) is an established paradigm -- exactly the setting TraLO's prediction-count constraints operate in.
